answers.explanation: The device accesses memory directly, without the CPU copying each byte.
A fast disk or network card would swamp the CPU with per-byte interrupts.
The controller interrupts once, when the whole block has been moved.
The controller copies the block straight to memory, without CPU intervention.
With the buffer address and the count, the controller can do the rest by itself.
John von Neumann described it in 1945. Nearly every computer today follows it.
That's the point: the CPU and device work in parallel.
